Confirmed this is actively causing multi-GB memory spikes. Concrete example:

A planning-only session in `~/agent-c/telemetry` that wrote 3 markdown files had a **115MB session_diff** with 22 entries — none from this session:

```
10365KB  meta/internal_tools/monty/app/api/agar/product_titles.json
 8782KB  tasks/optium-linkedin-creds/cross_environment/malicious_websites/lncdn.net%2F...
 8677KB  environments/linkedin.com/public/feed/styles/inline.css
 6990KB  environments/linkedin.com/reference.html
```

All status `added` — files committed by other agents between the session's start and current HEAD. The session touched none of them.

This compounds with #17622 (full file contents in before/after): `diffFull()` stores the complete body of every file in the worktree-global diff, including multi-MB test fixtures from other sessions.

In our environment (jj colocated repos, ~100 concurrent agent sessions), this produces **44GB of session_diff storage** and causes immediate multi-GB RSS spikes on session resume.

Review guide for this PR:

This PR is intentionally **core-only**. It does **not** contain the Postgres implementation; that lives in the external plugin PR at https://github.com/sjawhar/opencode-postgres-sync/pull/1.

Please focus review on three things:
1. **Local runtime changes** — per-session-tree SQLite sharding and the read/write routing changes in `packages/opencode/src/session/*`, `src/storage/db.ts`, and `src/sync/*`
2. **Plugin hook surface** — the new session hooks added to `packages/plugin/src/index.ts` and invoked from `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/session.ts`
3. **Minimal schema additions** — migrations and session metadata needed to support external resume-aware plugins

[FEATURE]: Extensible Tool Rendering System for TUI
**Summary**
Introduce an extensible tool rendering system in the TUI to allow plugins to define custom UI for their tools, similar to the web UI’s ToolRegistry.
**Motivation**
Currently, the TUI uses a hardcoded switch-based renderer. Plugin tools fall back to a generic text-based output with no interactivity or customization.
**Limitations:**
No way for plugins to customize tool rendering
No support for interactive behaviors (e.g., click navigation)
Metadata (e.g., sessionId) is ignored in rendering
Inconsistent behavior compared to the web UI
Proposed Solution
Provide extensibility through one or more of the following:
Tool Registry (Preferred)
Add a registry in the TUI where plugins can register custom renderers per tool:
ToolRegistry.register({
  name: "my_tool",
  render(props) {
    // custom TUI renderer
  }
});
Metadata-aware Generic Renderer (Minimal Fix)
Enhance the default renderer:
If metadata.sessionId exists → make the tool clickable
Enable navigation to the related session
Plugin Rendering Slot
Introduce a plugin hook/slot to inject custom UI into tool rendering
**Benefits**

- Enables full plugin extensibility in TUI
- Brings feature parity with web UI
- Supports interactive and metadata-driven rendering
- Improves developer experience for plugin authors
- Trade-offs
- Slight increase in complexity in the TUI rendering layer
- Need to maintain backward compatibility with existing tools
- Implementation Plan
- Introduce a Tool Registry in TUI
- Add fallback to GenericTool if no custom renderer exists
- Enhance GenericTool with basic metadata handling
- Expose plugin API for registration
- Add examples and documentation
- Self-Service

I am willing to work on an initial implementation, starting with the metadata-based enhancement and extending it to a full registry system.

Summary
Fix a runtime error in opentui caused by accessing .length on an undefined signal (list2()), which leads to application crashes.
Problem
In some cases, list2() is undefined (e.g., uninitialized state or async data not yet loaded). Accessing list2().length results in:
TypeError: undefined is not an object
Proposed Solution
Add a safe fallback when accessing list2():
(list2() ?? []).length
or
list2()?.length ?? 0
Additionally, ensure signals are initialized with default values where possible.
Impact
Prevents runtime crashes
Improves stability of the TUI
Ensures safe handling of undefined state
Implementation
Update all unsafe usages of list2().length with safe checks and optionally initialize the signal with an empty array.

Investigation update: I reproduced the stale `busy` lifecycle risk around session status transitions and am preparing a surgical fix focused on terminal-state cleanup (`idle`) across completion/error/abort paths, plus regression coverage in the existing session prompt/processor tests. I’ll post a follow-up with exact files changed and validation results once tests pass.
I went back to version 1.3.10, and the issue is not there anymore.

Implemented and validated a targeted fix for stale `busy` status lifecycle:

### What changed
- `packages/opencode/src/session/status.ts`
  - `SessionStatus.set()` now mutates in-memory status state **before** publishing status bus events.
  - This guarantees terminal `idle` state is committed even if event publication fails/rejects.

- Added regression coverage:
  - `packages/opencode/test/session/status-effect.test.ts`
  - New test simulates `session.status` publish rejection on `idle` and verifies state is still `idle` afterward (prevents stale `busy`).

### Validation run
- `cd packages/opencode && bun typecheck` ✅
- `cd packages/opencode && bun test test/session/status-effect.test.ts` ✅

Note: Existing prompt/processor effect suites currently fail in this environment with a pre-existing `instance: No context found for instance` error unrelated to this change path.

```
proxy () {
        if [[ -z "$1" ]]
        then
                echo "Usage: proxy <command>"
                return 1
        fi
        mitmweb --listen-host 127.0.0.1 --listen-port 58888 --web-open-browser &> /dev/null &
        local pid=$!
        echo -n "Waiting for mitmweb..."
        while ! nc -z 127.0.0.1 58888 2> /dev/null
        do
                sleep 0.2
        done
        echo " ready"
        export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="/Users/$USER/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem"
        export HTTPS_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:58888"
        export HTTP_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:58888"
        export NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1"
        "$@"
        kill "$pid" 2> /dev/null
        wait "$pid" 2> /dev/null
        unset NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY NO_PROXY
}
```
